title: Chief Mrs. Monica
fullName: Chief Mrs. Monica Edumongren Zisine Otoro
quote: Her love was gentle, her wisdom profound, and her memory still leads us home.
heroDescription: Her memory continues to shine in the hearts of her family and community. We remember her for the love, grace, strength, and faith that shaped her life and comforted all who knew her.
intro: Her story is one of resilience, sacrifice, and enduring Christian character. Through marriage, family life, industry, and service to others, she became a beloved matriarch whose legacy continues to live in the hearts of her children, grandchildren, and community.

storySections.heading: Her origins
storySections.body: Late Chief Mrs. Monica Edumongren Otoro hailed from Opululou of Ogodobiri, both paternally and maternally, in Bomadi Local Government Area of Delta State. She was the last child of Mr. and Mrs. Younburu Terebo, who were blessed with four children, three daughters and one son. Her eldest sister, Afa, was married to Gbagberi-Eyegha of Ayakoromo, while her immediate elder brother, Ebika-Ake, was also part of the family. Her other sister, Veronica, was married to Peter Perekeme of Ogodobiri.

storySections.heading: Marriage journey
storySections.body: Monica later married Chief Gabriel Zisine Otoro of Enekorogha, of the Eyo-Ioware family in Burutu Local Government Area. Through the intervention of Catechist Matthew Agbegha, a respected relative and Catholic catechist, the marriage journey began. Despite initial hesitation, persistence, counsel, and prayer led to their union, and this marriage became the foundation of a strong family life.

storySections.heading: Life of work and industry
storySections.body: Late Chief Mrs. Monica Otoro was a remarkably hardworking and industrious woman. She stood firmly beside her husband and accompanied him to different places of work, including palm-wine tapping and timber-related activities in Ekumu forest and Egra-bou in Ekogbene, as well as Seimogbene and Enekorogha. Her role in fetching firewood and cooking palm wine for ogogoro production was significant, and the family's livelihood depended greatly on her labour and commitment. She was also a seamstress, farmer, and fisherwoman, and she served her household with diligence and devotion.

storySections.heading: Christian faith and character
storySections.body: Late Chief Mrs. Monica Edumongren Zisine Otoro was a true Christian whose faith was evident in her life. She demonstrated love, humility, generosity, and forgiveness, and she was always ready to comfort others. Her kindness and concern for people earned her respect in Enekorogha and beyond. In her marriage, she was devoted to her husband and was a model of character, grace, and service within her family and community.

storySections.heading: Children and legacy
storySections.body: Late Chief Mrs. Monica Edumongren Zisine Otoro was blessed with children. She gave birth to nine children, comprising five daughters and three sons, with one pregnancy ending in miscarriage. Her children included Angelina, Roland, Very Rev. Father Dr. Victor, Mary, Helen, Lucy, and Gladys, among others. As a mother, Monica was deeply devoted to their upbringing and welfare. Her legacy continues through the good work she left behind: she was a devoted wife, loving mother, hardworking farmer and fisherwoman, skilled seamstress, supportive companion, committed Christian, and compassionate member of her community.
